                                                                                                                                         Turkey (EASE 2025). ACM, New York, NY, USA, 6 pages. https://doi.org/
                                         cation, existing testing approaches require developers to manually
                                                                                                                                         XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX
                                         write scripts using tools such as Appium and Espresso to execute
                                         the corresponding test case. This process is labor-intensive and de-
                                         mands significant effort to maintain as UI interfaces evolve through-
                                         out development. In this work, we introduce LELANTE, a novel
                                         framework that utilizes large language models (LLMs) to automate
                                         test case execution without requiring pre-written scripts. LELANTE
                                         interprets natural language test case descriptions, iteratively gener-
                                         ate action plans, and perform the actions directly on the Android
                                         screen using its GUI. LELANTE employs a screen refinement process
                                         to enhance LLM interpretability, constructs a structured prompt
                                         for LLMs, and implements an action generation mechanism based
                                         on chain-of-thought reasoning of LLMs. To further reduce com-
                                         putational cost and enhance scalability, LELANTE utilizes model
                                         distillation using a foundational LLM. In experiments across 390
                                         test cases spanning 10 popular Android applications, LELANTE
                                         achieved a 73% test execution success rate. Our results demon-
                                         strate that LLMs can effectively bridge the gap between natural
                                         language test case description and automated execution, making                                  Figure 1: Overview of the LELANTE test case execution pro-
                                         mobile testing more scalable and adaptable.                                                     cess. Given a natural language test case description, LELANTE
                                                                                                                                         incrementally refines the screen GUI representation and ex-
                                         CCS Concepts                                                                                    ecutes the test case step by step until completion.

backtracking, and inefficient execution paths, resulting in a fine-    Techniques and Models
tuning dataset consisting of 4,000 test case steps.
   For model adaptation, we employed Low-Rank Adaptation
(LoRA) [11], a parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach, allowing
us to optimize the model on local machines without excessive com-
putational overhead. Because we employ a step by step execution
model, we needed to train the model on the test steps rather than in
full execution history. Our fine-tuned model retained the structured
reasoning of the foundational model while significantly reducing
inference costs, making LELANTE more practical for real-world
deployment.

5    Related Works                                                       efficiency and adaptability to dynamic UI changes. Our work paves
Automated mobile application testing has traditionally relied on         the way for further advancements in AI-driven test automation, re-
script-based frameworks such as Appium and Espresso [3, 26], which       ducing developer effort, improving software quality and eliminating
allow developers to write scripts that simulate user interactions.       the need for manual script writing for test case automation. Future
While these tools provide consistency in test execution, they re-        efforts will focus on automating test outcome (i.e., expected results)
quire extensive manual effort to maintain scripts as applications        validation to reduce human dependency, optimizing backtracking
evolve, making them inefficient for large-scale automation. To miti-     performance, and investigating prompt-based or incremental learn-
gate script maintenance overhead, record-and-replay mechanisms,          ing techniques for leveraging historical execution data without
such as RERAN [15], capture user interactions for deterministic ex-      extensive model fine-tuning.
ecution. However, these approaches remain fragile when handling          8     Acknowledgments
